MERCURY <note>abbreviation for Mercurius/Hermes</note>

<margin>GENTILE MATTERS <note>original: "GENTILIA"</note></margin>

<margin>Jupiter.</margin>
<margin>Light.</margin>
<margin>Horoscopes.</margin>
<margin>All-forming <note>original: "Pantomorphos"</note>.</margin>

<meta>continues from previous page: and will mix itself with the liquids of its own source. Therefore, the leaders of all species are the gods.</meta> These gods are followed by the gods whose leader is <term>ousia</term> <gloss>essence or substance</gloss>. These are sensible gods, similar to their dual origin, who accomplish all things through sensible nature, each one illuminating his own work through another.

Of heaven, or whatever is understood by that name, the <term>ousiarches</term> <gloss>ruler of essence</gloss> is Jupiter. For through heaven, Jupiter provides life to all. Of the sun, the <term>ousiarches</term> is Light. For the good of Light is infused into us through the solar orb.

There are thirty-six (whose name is <term>Horoscopij</term> <gloss>Horoscopes, likely referring to the thirty-six decans of the zodiac</gloss>) of the stars always fixed in the same place; their <term>ousiarches</term> or leader is he whom they call <term>Pantomorphon</term> <gloss>the All-form</gloss>, who creates various forms for various species. 

The seven spheres which are called "erratic" <note>the seven wandering planets</note> have <term>ousiarchas</term>, that is, their own leaders, whom they call Fortune or <term>eimarmene</term> <gloss>Fate</gloss>. By these, all things are changed by the most firm stability of the law of nature, varied by eternal movement. 

Air, however, is the organ or machine of all things, through which all things are made. Its <term>ousiarches</term> is the second <note>a secondary creative power or the Demiurge</note>. It provides mortal things to mortals and similar things to these. 

Since these things are thus, moving from the lowest to the highest, all things are naturally connected to each other; so that mortal things are annexed to mortals, and sensible things to sensibles. The height of governance obeys that highest Lord, so that they are not many, or rather, they are one. For all things hang from one, or rather flow from him. When they are seen with distance, they are believed to be many things separately. But when unified they are one, or rather two, from which all things are made and by whom they are made: that is, from the matter from which they are made, and from his will, by whose nod they are brought about.

ASCLEPIUS: What is this reason again, O Trismegistus?
TRISMEGISTUS: Such it is, O Asclepius. For God, or the Father, or the Lord...

<summary>This page describes the hierarchy of divine rulers (ousiarches) who govern heaven, the sun, the zodiacal decans, and the planets. It establishes that while the universe appears diverse, all things are unified under the singular will of God and the principle of matter.</summary>
<keywords>Ousia, Ousiarches, Jupiter, Sun, Decans, Pantomorphos, Fate, Eimarmene, Divine Unity, Matter</keywords>
